title: The Weight of Copper: Riga, Amsterdam, and the First Banknotes in Europe
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Merchant's Son on the Daugava

stops.name: Riga, St. Peter's parish: the birth of Hans Witmacker
stops.date_confidence: Day attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon. The parish is reconstructed from the family's German Lutheran merchant standing and is documented nowhere. There is no canonical atlas Riga pin to inherit: richard_wagner and edward_witten hold Riga stops at two different coordinates, and kant and max_weber name the city in prose without a pin.
stops.campa: A son is born to the merchant Reinholdt Witmacker and Anna Bjelska in Riga, and they name him Hans. The city belongs to the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth this year and will belong to Sweden before he is ten, so the crown he is born under is not the crown that will ennoble him, sentence him, and outlive his bank. Riga is a Hanseatic town of grain, timber and credit, and the boy grows up inside the trade. The atlas reaches this city twice already, for Richard Wagner conducting its German theatre and for Edward Witten receiving a prize in it. Palmstruch stands two centuries in front of them both.
suggested_refs: St. Peter's Church, Riga, the German merchant parish of the Hanseatic town

stops.name: Riga, Ratslaukums: the house in the merchant quarter
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The father's occupation is attested; no document places the family in this square, and the year is a placement inside the childhood rather than a record of anything.
stops.campa: Around the town hall square stand the houses of the men who move Riga's goods, and Reinholdt Witmacker trades among them. Anna Bjelska is recorded as of Ruthenian descent, possibly of Jewish heritage, which ties the household eastward into the Commonwealth as firmly as the harbour ties it west. No source consulted names her town, her region, or her family. The son learns two directions at once: the Baltic road out to Lubeck and Amsterdam, and the river road inland toward the grain that comes down to the quays.
suggested_refs: The merchant houses of the Riga town hall square in the early seventeenth century

stops.name: Riga, the Great Guild: the institution the family belongs to
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction entirely. The father's merchant occupation is attested; no document ties either father or son to the Great Guild by name. The stop marks the institutional world of the trade and not a recorded visit. The year is a placement.
stops.campa: German merchant trade in Riga runs through the Great Guild, which settles who may buy, who may sell, and on whose word a bill is good. A merchant's son grows up inside its calendar whether or not his name is ever written in its book. Nothing survives to say the Witmackers were members. The guild exists to protect one proposition: a piece of paper carrying a trusted name is money, and the name is the part that can fail. He grows up inside that proposition years before he has any use for it.
suggested_refs: The Great Guild hall of Riga, governing body of the German merchant trade

stops.name: Riga, the Daugava harbour: the ship out
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. en.wikipedia gives only 'moved to Amsterdam around 1634' and describes no route; departure by ship down the Daugava is reconstructed from ordinary Baltic-to-Amsterdam practice. The year is a placement before that arrival.
stops.campa: He goes down the river and out past the bar into the Baltic, bound for the port that holds the credit of Europe. The Daugava carries the timber trade out and the sons of the trade with it. Riga can make a merchant; Amsterdam can make a banker, and the difference is what he is going to find out. He leaves as Hans Witmacker, a name that will be exchanged for another one in Stockholm, in a document he has not yet done anything to earn. No source records the ship, the month, or who paid for the passage.
suggested_refs: The Daugava river harbour of Riga and the Baltic sailings to the Dutch Republic

stops.name: Amsterdam, the IJ: arrival in the Dutch Republic
stops.date_confidence: en.wikipedia gives c. 1634 for the move; Svenskt biografiskt lexikon dates the move and the citizenship together to 1635. The one-year gap is not resolved. Coordinates: the atlas holds two Amsterdam pins, 52.3676/4.9041 (used by john_locke and annotated there as the canonical pin) and 52.3738/4.891 (william_paterson). The Locke value is used here; the conflict is recorded in the report, not silently settled.
stops.campa: He arrives at the busiest harbour in the world in the middle of the Dutch Golden Age. Ships from the Baltic unload the grain his father's city ships. The bank on the Dam settles the accounts of merchants who never touch a coin. Shares in a company that governs islands change hands daily on the Rokin. Everything Sweden lacks stands here in brick and is already a generation old. John Locke will hide in this city for five years, half a century after Witmacker walks into it, and finish a book about a mind that holds nothing it did not receive.
suggested_refs: The IJ waterfront and the Damrak, landing point of Baltic shipping at Amsterdam

stops.name: Amsterdam, the Stadhuis on the Dam: the burgher's oath
stops.date_confidence: Citizenship year attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon and en.wikipedia; month unknown, defaulted. Registration at the city hall is the standard procedure of the period and is reconstructed. The medieval Stadhuis on the Dam is meant, not the later palace built on the site.
stops.campa: He takes the citizenship of Amsterdam and with it the right to trade in his own name, to sue and to be sued, to borrow. The register of poorterschap is kept at the city hall on the Dam, and that is where such an oath is sworn. A Riga merchant's son becomes a burgher of the Dutch Republic at twenty-four. The rights arrive with an exposure he has not measured: credit extended in this city is extended against the person, and the person can be held. Four years from now the city will hold him for seven.
suggested_refs: The poorterboeken of Amsterdam, register of citizens admitted in 1635

stops.name: Amsterdam, the Beurs of Hendrick de Keyser: the apparatus of paper
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction as to his personal use of the exchange, which no source documents; what is attested is that Swedish sources describe Stockholms Banco as built on the Amsterdam model. The building of 1608-1611 is the first purpose-built stock exchange, not the first purpose-built exchange, which is Antwerp's Handelsbeurs of 1531; the research pool's claim of a world first is corrected. Coordinate corrected about 190 m northwest of the pool's value.
stops.campa: Over the Rokin stands the exchange, and near it the Wisselbank, taking deposits and settling by transfer in a ledger so that the metal itself need never move. Paper stands for silver here and is accepted as silver, because the city stands behind it. Twenty years from now Palmstruch will lay this arrangement in front of a Swedish king as though it were obvious. William Paterson will come to the same city in 1686 to be told no, and will build the English version anyway in 1694. The Swede reaches the model first and breaks it first.
suggested_refs: The Wisselbank of Amsterdam, founded 1609, and the Beurs van Hendrick de Keyser on the Rokin

stops.name: Amsterdam, the Oude Kerk quarter: the road south in August
stops.date_confidence: The August 1637 departure on an extended continental business journey is attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon; no itinerary survives and the day is unknown. Paris was checked as a canonical atlas pin (48.8566, 2.3522) and found unsupported by anything in the record. The quarter is a reconstruction from the standard geography of Amsterdam's Baltic trade.
stops.campa: His business runs where a Riga man's business would run, in the grain and commodity network behind the Oude Kerk, his father's trade continued in a larger room. In August he sets out on a long journey through the Continent. The source gives the month and nothing else: no towns, no partners, no cargo, no date of return. Whatever he contracts on that road is what he will be arrested for on the way back into the city, and the record of that has not survived either.
suggested_refs: The Baltic grain and commodity quarter behind the Oude Kerk, Amsterdam

stops.name: Amsterdam, the prison whose name is not recorded
stops.date_confidence: February 1639 attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon; day unknown. The cause is contested and left contested: de.wikipedia gives the same year and hedges it as allegedly unpaid debts, while SBL and sv.wikipedia record a disputed matter he maintained he was innocent of. The research pool stated the debt collapse as attested fact, which overstates every source. No source names the building; the pin marks the Rokin business district, not a confirmed prison.
stops.campa: He returns from the Continent in February and is taken into custody. The sources do not agree on why. One tradition says unpaid debts; the Swedish record says a commercial matter he insisted to the end he had no part in. They agree on the length. He is held seven years, and nothing consulted names the house that holds him, whether the Rasphuis or another of the city's correction buildings. The man who will invent a paper substitute for metal spends his thirties as a body held against a sum.
suggested_refs: The Rasphuis and the other Amsterdam correction houses, none of them named in the sources for this imprisonment

stops.name: Amsterdam, the Oude Kerk: a marriage and a baptism in one year
stops.date_confidence: Marriage in Amsterdam in February 1644 attested by en.wikipedia; day unknown. The wife's birth date of 30 December 1617 is from Svenskt biografiskt lexikon. The church of the marriage is not documented. The Oude Kerk is used because en.wikipedia records the couple's daughter baptized there in the same year; the research pool's guess of the Nieuwe Kerk is not followed, and its coordinate for that church was in any case about 90 m off.
stops.campa: In the fifth year of his confinement he marries Margrieta van der Bosch, whom Swedish records call Margareta von der Busch, born on the thirtieth of December 1617. A daughter is baptized in the same city in the same year. The marriage outlasts the prison, the ennoblement, the bank, the trial and the second imprisonment, and she survives him by six years. How a man held seven years is married and fathers a child is explained by nothing consulted, and the arrangement is left exactly as the record leaves it.
suggested_refs: The baptismal register of the Oude Kerk, Amsterdam, 1644

stops.name: Amsterdam, the promotorial of Queen Christina
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon: 'Pa grundval av drottning Kristinas promotorial 18 juli 1646 frigavs han ur fangelset och flyttade till Sverige.' The research pool's claim that no source accounts for the release is wrong and is corrected in the report.
stops.campa: A letter arrives from a queen he has never met. Christina of Sweden issues a promotorial on his behalf on the eighteenth of July, and on that basis the prison opens. Sweden is short of men who understand credit and long on copper it cannot carry, so the letter is an investment. He owes his liberty to a Swedish crown before he has served it a single day, and six years from now he will lay his first banking plan in front of the same queen. Amsterdam gave him the model. It also handed him a debt to Stockholm.
suggested_refs: Queen Christina's promotorial of 18 July 1646, the document that opened the Amsterdam prison

stops.name: Amsterdam, the IJ: sailing for Sweden
stops.date_confidence: Svenskt biografiskt lexikon's own header reads 'flyttade till Sverige 47', and en.wikipedia also gives 1647. The research pool asserted an SBL-versus-Wikipedia conflict between 1646 and 1647; no such conflict exists. Month unknown, defaulted. Coordinates: the canonical Amsterdam pin as used by john_locke.
stops.campa: He leaves the city that taught him and jailed him, thirteen years after he entered it, carrying a decade of Dutch credit practice and nothing else that is recorded. He is thirty-six. Behind him stand the Wisselbank, the exchange, the discounted bill, the deposit that moves by a line in a ledger. Ahead stands a kingdom rich in copper and bound to metal, where a large payment is made by cart. He will spend the rest of his life fitting the first into the second.
suggested_refs: The Amsterdam sailings to Stockholm in the late 1640s

stops.name: Stockholm, Skeppsbron: landing in a copper kingdom
stops.date_confidence: Arrival year attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon and en.wikipedia; month unknown, defaulted. Skeppsbron as the landing quay is the standard seventeenth-century Stockholm harbour point and is reconstructed.
stops.campa: Every ship into Stockholm ties up along the quay under Gamla Stan, and he comes ashore there among the barrels and the plates. Sweden's currency is copper struck in slabs: a ten-daler plate weighs close to twenty kilograms, and any considerable sum requires a wagon and a team to move it across a town. The country is a great power with money it cannot lift. He comes ashore carrying the Amsterdam arrangement in his head, and nine years pass before anybody in Stockholm will let him try it.
suggested_refs: Skeppsbron, the Stockholm quay of the Gamla Stan waterfront

stops.name: Täby, Gribbylund: the country house
stops.date_confidence: sv.wikipedia records the couple settling at Gribbylunds gard in Taby; the coordinate is from sv.wikipedia 'Gribbylund'. The research pool's value lay about 600 m east of the locality and is corrected. The year is a placement inside the Swedish period rather than a record.
stops.campa: North of the capital he takes the farm at Gribbylund and settles his wife and household there, an hour or so of road from the counting house. It is the property of a foreign merchant turning into a Swedish gentleman. A road in Taby still carries his name, and the parish church three and a half kilometres away will take his body. He holds the place through the ennoblement, the charter, the bank and the collapse, and the sentence that strips his title and his privilege reaches the estate too.
suggested_refs: Gribbylunds gard in Taby, and Palmstruchs vag named for him there

stops.name: Stockholm, Riddarhuset: the name Palmstruch
stops.date_confidence: Ennoblement on 18 June 1651, together with his brothers, attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon and sv.wikipedia. The venue is a reconstruction and a doubtful one: the Riddarhuset building was under construction from 1641 and not completed until 1660, so a ceremony inside it in 1651 is unlikely. The research pool's coordinate was about 300 m off and is corrected to the actual site.
stops.campa: On the eighteenth of June he and his brothers are ennobled, in recognition of merits their late father earned in a different country, and Hans Witmacker of Riga becomes Johan Palmstruch of Sweden. The name is six years old when the bank opens under it and seventeen when a court takes it away. The house of the nobility is still a building site in this year, and where the elevation was actually read out no reachable source says. The date is certain. So is the fact that the name was a gift.
suggested_refs: The Swedish letters of nobility of 18 June 1651 for the Witmacker brothers

stops.name: Stockholm, Tre Kronor: the first plan laid before Christina
stops.date_confidence: Attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon to 1652; month unknown, defaulted. Coordinates are the site of the Tre Kronor castle, which burned in 1697; the research pool's value fell on Storkyrkan and is corrected.
stops.campa: He brings his first banking plan to the queen whose letter opened his cell in Amsterdam six years earlier. Nothing comes of it. Christina's court is spending itself into difficulty on books and Latin and philosophers, and two winters earlier Rene Descartes died of the cold in this city, tutoring her before dawn. She does not found a bank. She abdicates in 1654 and leaves the kingdom, and Palmstruch has to begin the argument again with the man who follows her.
suggested_refs: Palmstruch's banking plan of 1652, submitted to Queen Christina

stops.name: Stockholm, Tre Kronor: commissioner of the Kommerskollegium
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon, 'eo kommissarie i Kommerskoll 16 mars 54'. The research pool flagged a contradiction with English sources dating the post to 1647; en.wikipedia dates no appointment at all, and the flagged contradiction does not exist. The Board's seat in the castle precinct is a reconstruction.
stops.campa: On the sixteenth of March he is made extraordinary commissioner at the Board of Trade, the crown office that regulates Swedish commerce. It is his first place inside the machine. Three years later he becomes ordinary commissioner, and he holds the post through the whole life of his bank, so that the man licensing trade and the man banking it are one man. Nobody in Stockholm remarks on this. The arrangement is not what destroys him; it is why nothing checks him.
suggested_refs: The Kommerskollegium of Sweden, founded 1651, and its commissioner rolls

stops.name: Stockholm, Stortorget: a bank proposed to the city
stops.date_confidence: Attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon to 1655; month unknown, defaulted. Stortorget as the seat of the city's radhus is a reconstruction: the source names the proposal, not the room it was heard in.
stops.campa: He proposes that Stockholm found a municipal bank, as Amsterdam did in 1609, with the city standing behind the deposits. The city does not take it. That refusal decides the shape of everything after: denied a bank owned by a town, he goes to a bank chartered by a king and owned in part by himself, with the crown taking half the profit. The distance between the two is one flight of stairs in the same quarter. A municipal bank could have failed quietly. A royal one fails in a courtroom.
suggested_refs: Palmstruch's 1655 proposal for a municipal bank of Stockholm

stops.name: Stockholm, Tre Kronor: the proposal to Charles X Gustav
stops.date_confidence: Attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon and sv.wikipedia to 1656; month unknown, defaulted. The castle as the seat of the royal council is a reconstruction.
stops.campa: He goes over the city's head to the king. Charles X Gustav is at war in Poland and needs money faster than copper can travel, which is the argument Palmstruch has been making since 1652 to men who did not yet need it. The plan is two banks: an exchange bank taking deposits for a fee and paying no interest, and a loans bank lending against property. His brother-in-law Reinhold Rademacher stands in the partnership. In Vienna in these same decades Samuel Oppenheimer will fund an emperor's wars on his own person and fortune. Palmstruch offers a king an institution instead of a man.
suggested_refs: The 1656 petition to Charles X Gustav for an exchange bank and a loans bank

stops.name: Stockholm, Tre Kronor: the charter of 30 November
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon ('k oktroj 30 nov') and by en.wikipedia 'Stockholms Banco', which gives the same date. The research pool wrote that the bank opened a full year later; it opened in July 1657, eight months later.
stops.campa: The royal charter is confirmed on the last day of November. Palmstruch has a privilege to run an exchange bank and a loans bank, the crown has half the profit, and Sweden has an instrument for the money it has been carrying in slabs. Eight months of fitting out follow. Twelve years later, almost to the season, a court will take this privilege back and hand it to the Estates of the realm, who will keep it for three and a half centuries and count their own founding from the day they took it.
suggested_refs: The royal oktroj of 30 November 1656 for Stockholms Banco

stops.name: Stockholm, Västerlånggatan: the exchange bank opens
stops.date_confidence: July 1657 attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon and en.wikipedia; day unknown, defaulted. The address is attested by SBL: 'P skaffade sin bank ett centralt affarslage i Sthlm i en fastighet vid Vasterlanggatan.' The research pool placed the bank at Jarntorget in four separate entries, which SBL contradicts; the coordinate here is approximate within the street.
stops.campa: The vaxelbank opens in a property on Vasterlanggatan, the trading street through the old town, taking deposits for a fee and paying no interest on them. Palmstruch is its director. In the same year he is promoted to ordinary commissioner at the Board of Trade. The bank does not stand on Jarntorget, where a later tradition puts it. That square belongs to the Riksbank's own building, raised in the 1680s by the institution that inherited his privilege after taking it away from him.
suggested_refs: The premises of Stockholms Banco on Vasterlanggatan, Gamla Stan

stops.name: Stockholm, Västerlånggatan: the loans bank and the merger
stops.date_confidence: Spring 1659 attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon and en.wikipedia; no exact date is given and the month is defaulted.
stops.campa: In the spring the lanebank opens, lending against property, and the two halves are joined into Stockholms Banco with Palmstruch as general manager. The design is Amsterdam's split in two: a deposit bank that holds and transfers, a lending bank that puts money out. In Amsterdam the two were kept apart on purpose. Here they sit in one house under one man, and the deposits of the first become the reserve against which the second lends. That is the whole mechanism of what follows, and it is in place two years before a single note is printed.
suggested_refs: The lanebank of 1659 and its merger into Stockholms Banco

stops.name: Stockholm, Västerlånggatan: four hundred thousand in, eight hundred thousand out
stops.date_confidence: Attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon; month unknown, defaulted. The figures are SBL's: deposits above 400,000 daler kopparmynt against gross lending of roughly 830,000.
stops.campa: Deposits pass four hundred thousand daler kopparmynt. Gross lending reaches about eight hundred and thirty thousand. The bank is lending twice what it holds, in a currency whose unit is a copper slab, to a country at war. The numbers are not concealed anywhere; they are what the office writes down. Nobody in Stockholm has a word yet for the condition they describe, and the man running the bank is also the crown's commissioner of trade, so there is no second desk where they might be read differently.
suggested_refs: The 1660 balance of Stockholms Banco as summarized in Svenskt biografiskt lexikon

stops.name: Stockholm, the coin is thinned
stops.date_confidence: The reduction of roughly 17 per cent in the copper content of the coinage, and the resulting wave of withdrawal demands, are attested by en.wikipedia 'Stockholms Banco' to 1660; month unknown, defaulted. Coordinates: the canonical atlas Stockholm pin, inherited byte-identical from hilma_af_klint and miranda.
stops.campa: The crown reduces the copper in the coinage by about a sixth. Every depositor works out in the same week that the plates he handed in were heavier than the plates he will be handed back, and comes to the counter to take his money out while it is still the money he deposited. The bank has lent it. This is the first run, and it happens before the banknotes exist: paper is not the cause of it, paper is the answer Palmstruch reaches for. He has eighteen months to find it.
suggested_refs: The Swedish coinage reduction of 1660 and the first run on Stockholms Banco

stops.name: Stockholm, Västerlånggatan: the first banknotes in Europe
stops.date_confidence: July 1661 attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon and by en.wikipedia in both the 'Johan Palmstruch' and 'Stockholms Banco' articles; day unknown, defaulted. The quote is a museum paraphrase of his motive, verified on the page cited, and is not his own words.
stops.campa: In July the bank issues kreditivsedlar in denominations of five, twenty-five, one hundred and one thousand daler kopparmynt, signed by hand by the director and his clerks. They are the first banknotes issued by a bank in Europe. A sum that needed a cart now goes in a coat. They are not receipts for particular deposits; they are the bank's promise, in fixed amounts, and they circulate on the promise alone. For rather more than two years they work exactly as intended.
stops.quote: bankdirektören Johan Palmstruch redan från början ville ersätta de stora plåtmynten med sedlar eftersom de var lättare att hantera
stops.quote_source: Ekonomiska museet (Swedish Museum of Finance), 'Europas första banksedlar', ekonomiskamuseet.se; a museum paraphrase of Palmstruch's motive, not a quotation of him
suggested_refs: Surviving kreditivsedlar of Stockholms Banco, 1661-1664, in Swedish numismatic collections

stops.name: Göteborg, an exchange agent and no branch
stops.date_confidence: sv.wikipedia says the business went so well that offices were opened in Goteborg, Falun and Abo. Svenskt biografiskt lexikon rejects exactly that: 'I Gbg fanns endast ett vaxlingsombud.' An exchange agent, not a branch. The research pool carried the sv.wikipedia version as attested; it is downgraded here to tradition. The year and the Kronhuset coordinate are both reconstructions.
stops.campa: In Sweden's Atlantic port the bank has an exchange agent and nothing more. A tradition grew up that Palmstruch was building a national branch network out of Stockholm, Goteborg, Falun and Abo, and the Swedish biographical lexicon calls that tradition hardly correct. What stands in Goteborg is one man changing money at a counter. The branch network lives in the retelling and not in the record, and the retelling is three centuries younger than the thing it describes.
suggested_refs: The Kronhuset quarter of Goteborg, seventeenth-century civic centre of the town

stops.name: Falun, the branch that was not built
stops.date_confidence: Attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon that the branch was planned and never established: 'I Falun motte P misstro, och den planerade filialen dar kom inte till stand.' The year is a placement inside the note-issuing period; the coordinate is the town, not a premises.
stops.campa: At Falun the copper comes out of the ground. The Stora Kopparberg mine is the source of the metal the whole scheme exists to replace, and the men who own it meet the banker with distrust. The branch is planned and never opened. Their refusal is exact in its logic: paper standing for copper is a claim on copper, and the people who dig the copper can see what a claim is worth on the day there are more claims than there is metal. They are right two years early.
suggested_refs: The Stora Kopparberg mine at Falun, source of the plate money's metal

stops.name: Åbo, what is not known
stops.date_confidence: Included as a stated gap. sv.wikipedia lists Abo among the bank's offices; Svenskt biografiskt lexikon answers 'Vad som hande i Abo ar okant', what happened in Abo is unknown. The year is a placement and the coordinate is the town.
stops.campa: Across the Gulf of Bothnia lies the Finnish half of the kingdom and its chief town. Swedish tradition lists Abo among the bank's offices. The Swedish biographical lexicon answers in five words that what happened in Abo is unknown. No agent is named, no premises, no date, no sum. The stop stands here because the claim is in circulation and the evidence for it is not, and an atlas that quietly dropped the town would leave the tradition standing unopposed.
suggested_refs: Abo, chief town of the Finnish half of the Swedish realm in the 1660s

stops.name: Stockholm, Västerlånggatan: the paper outruns the metal
stops.date_confidence: Attested by en.wikipedia 'Stockholms Banco' to 1663; month unknown, defaulted.
stops.campa: Lending goes on expanding and the notes are printed to fund it. Nothing in the charter fixes how many notes may stand against how much metal, because no such rule has been written yet by anybody: the instrument is two years old and Palmstruch invented it. By autumn the notes are trading below their face. There is no Swedish word for the thing either. People do not name it. They walk to Vasterlanggatan with the paper in hand and ask for the copper.
suggested_refs: The 1663 over-issue of kreditivsedlar against the bank's metal reserve

stops.name: Stockholm, Västerlånggatan: from October the bank refuses
stops.date_confidence: October 1663 attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon, 'Fran oktober manad maste den i vaxande omfattning vagra att inlosa de kreditivsedlar som kom in', and, contrary to the research pool's claim of a source conflict, by en.wikipedia 'Stockholms Banco' as well. Both say October 1663. Day unknown, defaulted.
stops.campa: From October the bank must increasingly refuse to redeem the notes brought to it. The promise printed on the paper and signed by the director is not met at the counter where the director sits. A note that cannot be exchanged for the thing it names is a piece of paper with a name on it, and the whole distance between money and paper, which the bank existed to abolish, reappears in a single autumn. Twenty-six months separate the first issue from the first refusal.
suggested_refs: The October 1663 suspension of redemption at Stockholms Banco

stops.name: Stockholm, Tre Kronor: the notes prohibited and a commission named
stops.date_confidence: Attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon and sv.wikipedia to 1664; month unknown, defaulted. Operations cease in 1664 and liquidation completes in 1667; the research pool's phrase 'the bank fails in 1668' conflates both of those with the year of the verdict.
stops.campa: Government and Riksdag prohibit the notes once their value has fallen far enough, and the bank's operations stop. A commission of the riksrad is appointed to establish what happened. It sits for three years. Palmstruch is not yet accused of anything: he is the director of a closed bank, still a nobleman, still a commissioner of the Board of Trade, waiting while other men read his ledgers. The instrument he invented is now illegal in the kingdom that chartered it.
suggested_refs: The riksrad commission of 1664 into the affairs of Stockholms Banco

stops.name: Stockholm, the second series that may not exist
stops.date_confidence: Open contradiction, not resolved. en.wikipedia describes a 1666 series of 10, 25, 50 and 100 silver daler called Palmstruchare. sv.wikipedia 'Kreditivsedel' says notes were issued 'fran 1661 till 1666'. sv.wikipedia 'Stockholms Banco' says only 1661-1664 and mentions neither the series nor the term. Svenskt biografiskt lexikon has operations ceasing in 1664 and records instead that Palmstruch sat on the crown's coinage commissions in September and October 1666. Coordinates: the canonical atlas Stockholm pin.
stops.campa: One tradition holds that a second series of notes appears in this year, denominated in silver daler and called Palmstruchare after him. Another says the issues ran from 1661 to 1666. A third says 1661 to 1664, and the biographical lexicon has the bank shut since 1664, which would put a new issue two years after the notes were banned. What the lexicon does record for 1666 is Palmstruch sitting on the crown's coinage commissions in September and October. The atlas keeps all four statements and settles none of them.
suggested_refs: The disputed 1666 silver-daler series known as Palmstruchare

stops.name: Stockholm, Västerlånggatan: the last note redeemed
stops.date_confidence: Attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon that the liquidation completed in 1667 with the redemption of the last outstanding credit note; month unknown, defaulted.
stops.campa: The liquidation finishes when the last outstanding kreditivsedel is brought in and paid. Every note the bank ever issued is accounted for, six years after the first of them was signed by hand. The house on Vasterlanggatan holds no deposits and makes no loans. What remains of Stockholms Banco is a privilege on paper, a deficit, and a director who has spent eleven years arguing that paper can stand for metal and has just demonstrated, at the scale of a kingdom, the precise conditions under which it cannot.
suggested_refs: The 1667 liquidation accounts of Stockholms Banco

stops.name: Stockholm, Tre Kronor: the council sends him to the Svea hovrätt
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon: the commission appointed in 1664 concluded in 1667, and the council resolved on 2 May 1667 to hold Palmstruch answerable before the Svea hovratt.
stops.campa: The commission finishes its three years of reading and the council of the realm resolves, on the second of May, to put Palmstruch before the Svea court of appeal. He has by this point already been in custody for some time. The Swedish record says he had been held for several years when judgment finally came, and does not say when it began. The decision to prosecute is dated to the day. The start of the imprisonment is not, and nothing consulted supplies it.
suggested_refs: The riksrad resolution of 2 May 1667 committing Palmstruch to the Svea hovratt

stops.name: Stockholm, Tre Kronor: the verdict of 22 July
stops.date_confidence: Attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon, whose 'Domen foll 22 juli foljande ar' follows the council's decision of 2 May 1667, and by en.wikipedia; the two agree on 1668. The research pool dated the verdict 22 July 1667 and invented a conflict between the sources, which the report records. Venue is a reconstruction: the Svea hovratt sat in the royal castle in 1668, not at the Wrangelska palatset on Riddarholmen, which it occupied only in the following century.
stops.campa: The Svea court of appeal sentences him on the twenty-second of July to removal from office, forfeiture of the privilege to conduct banking, and perpetual banishment from the kingdom, the sentence convertible to death if the damages go unpaid. Seventeen years separate the ennoblement from the verdict. The court takes back the office, the privilege and the country. The name Palmstruch, given in 1651 for his father's merits, is the last item on the list and it goes with the rest.
suggested_refs: The judgment of the Svea hovratt, 22 July 1668

stops.name: Stockholm, the privilege passes to the Estates
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by en.wikipedia 'Stockholms Banco'. Coordinates: the canonical atlas Stockholm pin, inherited byte-identical from hilma_af_klint and miranda.
stops.campa: Eight weeks after the verdict the banking privilege is transferred to Riksens Standers Bank, the bank of the Estates of the realm, answerable to the Riksdag and not to the crown. It is the direct ancestor of Sveriges Riksbank and is generally called the oldest central bank in the world. It begins by taking a convicted man's charter and running it under supervision. Sweden does not abolish what Palmstruch built. It takes the thing away from him and keeps it.
suggested_refs: The transfer of the banking privilege to Riksens Standers Bank, 17 September 1668

stops.name: Stockholm, Gamla Stan: the prison whose name is not recorded
stops.date_confidence: The fact and the end of the custody are attested; the beginning is not. sv.wikipedia 'Stockholms Banco' says he had already been imprisoned for several years when judgment fell in 1668, and Svenskt biografiskt lexikon fixes only the end, 'holls i fangsligt forvar till 1670'. The research pool's 1668-1670 span understates it. No source names the prison. Coordinates: the Gamla Stan pin inherited byte-identical from jules_verne.
stops.campa: He is held somewhere in the old town, and nothing consulted names the building, the room, or the year he entered it. Twice in one life he is imprisoned in a city he came to as a foreigner, once in Amsterdam for seven years and once here for a number nobody wrote down. The second confinement runs through the trial rather than after it. A man convicted in July 1668 has by then already been sitting for years in the custody of the state whose money he had tried to make lighter.
suggested_refs: The prisons of seventeenth-century Gamla Stan, none of them named in the sources for this custody

stops.name: Stockholm, the reprieve of 26 February
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon. The death penalty was contingent on the unpaid damages from the moment of sentencing rather than being commuted at it; the council lifted the contingency at this session. Venue reconstructed as the council's seat in the royal castle.
stops.campa: The council lifts the death penalty. It had never been a sentence of death outright, only a sentence that turned into one if the deficit went unpaid, and the deficit is not going to be paid by a man who has nothing. So the condition is struck out. Twenty-three years earlier a Swedish queen's letter had opened a Dutch prison for him. He keeps his life and stays in custody, without office, without privilege, without the title, under a standing order of banishment from a kingdom that will not let him leave.
suggested_refs: The council session of 26 February 1669 lifting the capital contingency

stops.name: Stockholm, Gamla Stan: released
stops.date_confidence: Attested by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon, 'holls i fangsligt forvar till 1670', and by sv.wikipedia; month unknown, defaulted. Coordinates: the Gamla Stan pin inherited byte-identical from jules_verne.
stops.campa: He is let out. He is fifty-nine and has under a year to live. The bank belongs to another institution, the notes are illegal, the title is gone, and the sentence of banishment stands on the books of a country he does not leave. Whether the pardon restored anything beyond his liberty, nothing consulted says. He goes back to his wife, and the parish that records his death the following March is the parish of the great church in the old town, a few minutes on foot from Vasterlanggatan.
suggested_refs: The 1670 release, recorded without a month in any reachable source

segments.name: Täby and the Bank That Outlived Him

stops.name: Stockholm, Storkyrkan parish: the death of 8 March
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon and en.wikipedia; the parish is Stockholms domkyrkoforsamling, the Storkyrkan parish of the old town.
stops.campa: He dies in the parish of the great church, sixty years old, eleven months out of custody. Fourteen years earlier he had opened the first bank in Sweden a few hundred metres from here, and ten years earlier he had signed by hand the first banknotes issued by any bank in Europe. In this same city, in this same decade, the institution holding his charter is learning to run it properly. The invention survives. The inventor is buried out of a parish register with no office to his name.
suggested_refs: The death register of Stockholms domkyrkoforsamling, March 1671

stops.name: Täby kyrka: the tombstone and the arms of 1671
stops.date_confidence: Burial at Taby Church attested by en.wikipedia; the burial date is given by no source consulted, and the month here is the house default rather than a record. Coordinate from sv.wikipedia 'Taby kyrka'; the research pool's afterlife lens gave a value about 5.4 km south, with the Stockholm longitude copied down the file, and that is corrected here. A tombstone and a coat of arms, both dated 1671, are photographed in the church; the inscription text and its present legibility are recorded nowhere reachable.
stops.campa: He is laid in the medieval stone church three and a half kilometres from Gribbylund, under walls painted by Albertus Pictor in the fifteenth century, among them Death sitting at the chessboard opposite a knight. A tombstone survives in the church and a coat of arms with it, both dated 1671, the arms of a nobility taken from him three years before he died. Nothing consulted transcribes what the stone says. The man who made money light lies under a heavy one, in a country parish, not in the capital.
suggested_refs: The Palmstruch tombstone and armorial at Taby Church, both dated 1671
Albertus Pictor's fifteenth-century paintings in Taby kyrka

stops.name: Stockholm, the widow
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by Svenskt biografiskt lexikon. Coordinates: the canonical atlas Stockholm pin, inherited byte-identical from hilma_af_klint and miranda.
stops.campa: Margareta von der Busch dies on the twentieth of March, six years after her husband. She married him in a prison year in Amsterdam and outlived the bank, the trial, the second imprisonment and the man. Nothing consulted records where she lived after 1671, what remained of the estate, or whether the damages were ever pursued against it. She is a date at each end and a name in the middle, which is more than the record gives their daughter, baptized in Amsterdam in 1644 and never mentioned again.
suggested_refs: Margareta von der Busch, born 30 December 1617, died 20 March 1677

stops.name: Grocers' Hall, Poultry: the charge stated in English
stops.date_confidence: The Bank of England's move to Grocers' Hall on 31 December 1694 and the prospectus sentence are attested in william_paterson.journey.json, from which the coordinate is inherited byte-identical. Palmstruch is named in no existing atlas file: the lineage drawn here is the atlas's own and is not stated by any source.
stops.campa: Twenty-three years after Palmstruch dies, a Scot who was refused in Amsterdam in 1686 opens the Bank of England and prints in its prospectus the sentence that describes exactly what happened on Vasterlanggatan. William Paterson has never heard the name. Two years later Isaac Newton is called to the Mint to rebuild the silver under the English paper, and John Locke, home from his Dutch exile, argues the same case from the Board of Trade. The line runs Amsterdam, Stockholm, London, and only the middle term went to prison for it.
stops.quote: All money or credit not having an intrinsic value, to answer the contents or denomination thereof, is false and counterfeit; and the loss must fall one where or other.
stops.quote_source: William Paterson, 'A Brief Account of the Intended Bank of England' (1694), in The Writings of William Paterson, ed. Saxe Bannister, 2nd ed. (1859), vol. III, p. 83, as carried in william_paterson.journey.json
sources: william_paterson.journey.json (stops 'Amsterdam, the Dutch Republic declines' and 'Grocers' Hall, Poultry: the Bank moves house')
suggested_refs: Grocers' Hall on Poultry, home of the Bank of England from 1694 to 1734

stops.name: Stockholm, the Riksbank counts from 1668
stops.date_confidence: The founding of Stiftelsen Riksbankens Jubileumsfond in 1962 against the tercentenary counted from 1668, confirmed by parliament on 2 December 1964, is attested by sv.wikipedia 'Riksbankens Jubileumsfond'; month of the 1962 founding unknown, defaulted. Coordinates: the canonical atlas Stockholm pin.
stops.campa: For its three hundredth anniversary the Riksbank endows a foundation for research in the humanities and the social sciences, and parliament confirms it on the second of December 1964. The three hundred years are counted from 1668, the year the Estates took the charter, and not from 1657, the year Palmstruch opened the doors. The oldest central bank in the world dates itself from the moment it removed its founder. He is credited with the invention in every account of it and with the institution in none.
suggested_refs: Stiftelsen Riksbankens Jubileumsfond, founded 1962, confirmed by the Riksdag 2 December 1964
